diagrams.title: How a rule travels (2004 → 2007 → 2017 → 2025 → today)
diagrams.caption: Tracing Floor Area Ratio (FAR) across twenty-two years and five instruments, with every step linked to its exact official PDF page.
diagrams.slideSummary: How FAR travels across five instruments (2004 → 2007 → 2017 → 2025 → today), with every step traced to its official page.
diagrams.presenterNotes: Follow how a single rule — Floor Area Ratio — travels across twenty-two years: 2004 Bye-laws Table 6, 2007 Master Plan Table 10, 2017 Bye-law 1.4 handing FAR to the Master Plan, April 2025 Chapter 11 adding Premium FAR and TDR, and what applies today.
diagrams.mermaid:
flowchart LR
  S1["2004 · Bye-laws 9.2 (Table 6, p. 21)"] --> S2["2007 · Master Plan Ch. 4 (Table 10, p. 28)"]
  S2 --> S3["2017 · Bye-law 1.4 Hand-off (UDD 14 TTP 2017, p. 2)"]
  S3 --> S4["2025 · Premium FAR Ch. 11 (Table 27, p. 2)"]
  S4 --> S5["Today · Base FAR + Premium FAR + TDR (Note 2, p. 3)"]

diagrams.title: The five data layers (sources → structure → rules as data → resolution → site)
diagrams.caption: From immutable official PDFs and SHA-256 digests to structured provisions, parameter records, six-step statutory resolution, and static web/AI endpoints.
diagrams.slideSummary: Five data layers turn official PDFs into structured provisions, condition-bearing parameter rows, six-step statutory resolution, and static web and AI views.
diagrams.presenterNotes: Every instrument passes through five data layers: (1) Sources with SHA-256 and Wayback snapshots, (2) Structure with {{provisions}} provisions and separate site notes, (3) Rules as data with {{rules_as_data}} active parameter rows, (4) Six-step statutory resolution, and (5) Static web, map, and AI endpoints.
diagrams.mermaid:
flowchart LR
  L1["1. Sources ({{registered_sources}} PDFs + SHA-256 + Wayback)"] --> L2["2. Structure ({{provisions}} provisions + tables)"]
  L2 --> L3["3. Rules as data ({{rules_as_data}} active parameter rows)"]
  L3 --> L4["4. Resolution (6-step statutory order)"]
  L4 --> L5["5. Site, Map & AI (/llms.txt · .md · /api/v1/)"]

diagrams.title: The checks pipeline ({{checks_per_build}} automatic build checks + workshop verification)
diagrams.caption: Every build runs {{checks_per_build}} automated verification suites; records reach person-verified status only after two independent workshop Match verdicts.
diagrams.slideSummary: Every build runs {{checks_per_build}} automated checks against stored PDF page text and bounds; two independent human Match verdicts promote a record to person-verified.
diagrams.presenterNotes: Trust comes from two verification levels: Level 1 runs {{checks_per_build}} automated checks on every build (text fidelity against stored PDF page text, hierarchy depth, parameter plausibility, band continuity, 5-corporation parity, map street-offset, provenance, plain language, licences, and WCAG AA budgets). Level 2 requires two independent workshop Match verdicts and zero Mismatches.
diagrams.mermaid:
flowchart LR
  A["Stored PDF Page Text & Schemas"] --> B["Level 1 · {{checks_per_build}} Automatic Build Checks ({{machine_checked}} records)"]
  B --> C["Workshop Task Set (/verify/<task-set>)"]
  C --> D{"2+ Independent Match & 0 Mismatch?"}
  D -->|"Yes"| E["Level 2 · Verified by a Person ({{verified_by_people}} records)"]
  D -->|"Mismatch"| F["Open Review Item (verification-review.md)"]

diagrams.title: Layered data packs: national → state → city (planned)
diagrams.caption: Planned pack architecture storing shared text once and recording whether each higher-tier rule is adopted, adopted with changes, or reference only.
diagrams.slideSummary: Planned layered packs (national → state → city) store shared text once and record whether each rule is adopted, adopted with changes, or reference only.
diagrams.presenterNotes: This diagram shows the planned layered pack architecture. National model codes and standards sit at the top, state Acts and model bye-laws sit in the middle, and city/corporation rules sit at the bottom. Each link explicitly states adopted, adopted with changes, or reference only.
diagrams.mermaid:
flowchart TD
  N["National Pack (Planned) · NBC 2016 & Aviation Reference"] -->|"Reference only (Rule R13)"| S["State Pack (Planned) · State Acts, Master Plan & Model Rules"]
  S -->|"Adopted / Adopted with changes (e.g. Bye-law 1.4)"| C["City Pack (Planned) · {{city}} & {{corporations}} City Corporations"]
  S -->|"Reference only (where not adopted by city)"| C

diagrams.title: The planned local agent engine and its four doors
diagrams.caption: Planned TypeScript engine running locally on the user's machine over downloadable packs, exposing MCP, CLI, Agent Skill, and open data files.
diagrams.slideSummary: The planned local TypeScript agent engine runs on the user's machine and exposes four doors: local MCP server, CLI, Agent Skill, and open data files.
diagrams.presenterNotes: Here are the four doors of the planned local TypeScript agent engine: Door 1 is a local MCP server for Claude, Cursor, VS Code, Gemini CLI, and Codex; Door 2 is a command-line tool; Door 3 is an Agent Skill teaching the four honesty rules; and Door 4 is the open data files themselves.
diagrams.mermaid:
flowchart TB
  P["Local Data Packs (Planned) + Offline Keyword & Meaning Search"] --> E["Bylaw One Local Agent Engine in TypeScript (Planned)"]
  E --> D1["Door 1 · Local MCP Server (Claude, Cursor, VS Code, Gemini CLI, Codex)"]
  E --> D2["Door 2 · Command Line (bylaws CLI for any agent)"]
  E --> D3["Door 3 · Agent Skill (Cite page · Label derived · Ask plot details · Confirm)"]
  P --> D4["Door 4 · Open Data Files (JSON · GeoJSON · Markdown · CC BY 4.0)"]
